resources.string: "No calibration override applied. Sensor values are used as-is. Use this when the sensor is already factory-calibrated and accurate."

"Per-sensor linear calibration override (slope and offset) computed from your fingerstick entries. Recent entries are weighted higher. Override is applied after the current sensor session start; first 2 hours are skipped as warm-up."
Possible sensor change detected at %1$s. Mark as new sensor?
Log a sensor change to enable calibration.
Fit out of safe range — calibration not applied.
Offset-only calibration applied — sensor range too narrow for slope.
Calibration applied — slope clamped to safe range. Add more entries to relax.
This will invalidate the entry. The fit will be recalculated.

Add a fingerstick calibration to activate sensor correction. For the best result: wait until warm-up is over, calibrate while your glucose is steady (not rising or falling fast), and use a fresh, careful meter reading. At least 2 calibrations are needed, ideally at different glucose levels.

Your recent calibrations gave an inconsistent result and are not applied — the sensor is showing uncorrected values. Add a new calibration while your glucose is steady; double-check your meter reading, since a single inaccurate fingerstick can throw this off.

Your calibrations are all close in glucose value, so only a basic correction can be applied. Add one the next time your glucose is clearly higher or lower than usual — spreading calibrations across different levels makes the correction accurate across your whole range, not just around one value.

It\'s been a while since your last calibration. Sensors can drift over their wear time, so adding a fresh calibration now — while your glucose is steady — helps keep the correction accurate for the rest of the session.
